data.name: Austria
data.summary: Austria taxes a resident's capital gains on securities and dividends at a flat 27.5% (bank interest 25%) regardless of holding period or size of holding, and real estate gains at 30%. There is no wealth tax and no inheritance or gift tax (abolished 2008), so children inherit a securities portfolio tax-free; only real estate passing within the family bears a stepped real estate transfer tax of 0.5%-3.5% plus a 1.1% registration fee, and larger lifetime gifts must be notified to the tax office. Emigration triggers a deemed sale of financial assets, deferred without interest for moves within the EU/EEA.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Unlimited liability on worldwide income for residents. Investment income is taxed at special flat rates (§ 27a EStG) that are final when withheld by an Austrian bank.
regimes.eligibility: A home (Wohnsitz) in Austria or habitual abode (stay of more than six months). Non-EU citizens need a residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on shares, bonds, funds and derivatives are taxed at a flat 27.5% (§ 27a(1) EStG) whatever the holding period and whatever the size of the shareholding, including substantial private-company stakes. Gains on private real estate are taxed at a flat 30% (§ 30a EStG); the main residence is exempt under conditions. There is no annual allowance.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: No allowance for capital income. Main residence exempt if lived in for 2 years since acquisition or 5 of the last 10 years. Shares bought before 2011 (bonds/derivatives before 30 March 2012) are grandfathered and tax-free, unless a holding of at least 1%.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Resident individual holding as private assets. Austrian banks withhold the 27.5% as a final tax; foreign accounts are declared in the return at the same rate. Option to be taxed at the regular progressive rate if lower (Regelbesteuerungsoption).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Losses can be offset only within the same year against other capital income (not against bank interest), and cannot be carried forward. Exit tax (§ 27(6) Z 1 EStG): leaving Austria is a deemed sale of all financial assets at market value; for a move to an EU/EEA state the tax is assessed but not collected until actual sale (annual proof required if relevant income exceeds EUR 100,000); a move outside the EU/EEA makes the tax due. Since 1 January 2025 a 30% surcharge applies to gains from land rezoned to building land.

sources.title: EStG 1988 § 30a (special rate on real estate gains)

open_questions: Main-residence exemption conditions and the 2025 rezoning surcharge were taken from general knowledge and a Deloitte search summary; the § 30 EStG text was not opened.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Securities and private business shares: the 27.5% special rate of § 27a(1) Z 2 EStG applies to all capital gains of private investors, with no surcharges and no holding-period relief. Real estate: 30% flat under § 30a(1) EStG. Foreign real estate: the 30% Austrian rate before treaty relief; most Austrian treaties leave real estate gains to the situs country (Austria then exempts or credits).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Low risk for securities: capital income of private investors stays under § 27 even with frequent trading. Commercial real estate dealing can turn real estate gains into business income at progressive rates (up to 55%).
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: None for securities acquired after 2010 (bonds/derivatives after 30 March 2012) or for real estate.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide taxation at the same rates; foreign accounts declared in the return. Foreign real estate gains depend on the treaty with the situs country.

dividends.summary: Dividends, domestic or foreign, are taxed at a flat 27.5%, withheld as a final tax by Austrian banks or declared in the return for foreign accounts. Foreign withholding tax is credited up to 15% via the Austrian custodian bank, regardless of the treaty.
dividends.eligibility_conditions: Private shareholder; option for progressive taxation if lower.
dividends.important_exceptions: Foreign withholding above 15% must be reclaimed from the source country.

sources.title: Körperschaftsteuergesetz 1988 § 24 (Abs. 5: credit of Zwischensteuer on distributions)

dividends.rate_basis: 27.5% special rate (§ 27a(1) Z 2 EStG); foreign dividends taxed at 27.5% of the gross amount with a credit for foreign withholding tax of at most 15%.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 27.5% KESt on dividends paid to individuals; 23% to corporations; reduced by treaties and to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
dividends.treaty_network: About 90 income tax treaties including the US and all EU states.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Dividends from Austrian and qualifying foreign participations held by an Austrian company are generally exempt; portfolio holdings in a GmbH are taxed at 23% and distributions again at 27.5%. No structure is modelled: from 2026 a Privatstiftung pays 27.5% interim tax on gains and interest (the same as a private investor; § 22(2) KStG), only defers tax on dividends until they are paid out at 27.5%, costs 3.5% entry tax on the endowment, and Austria has no inheritance tax to avoid; a GmbH (23% plus 27.5% on payout) is worse.

wealth_tax.summary: Austria has no wealth tax (net wealth tax not levied since 1994).
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: Reintroducing wealth and inheritance taxes is a recurring SPÖ demand; the 2025 coalition (ÖVP-SPÖ-NEOS) budget measures did not include one.
open_questions: The 1994 date of abolition is from general knowledge; the source only says there is no wealth tax.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal Grundsteuer based on the old assessed value (Einheitswert), at most 1% of assessed value; usually small.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance or gift tax since 1 August 2008. A securities portfolio passes to children tax-free. Real estate passing within the family bears real estate transfer tax on the property value at stepped rates (0.5% on the first EUR 250,000, 2% on the next EUR 150,000, 3.5% above), plus a 1.1% land-registry fee. Lifetime gifts of cash, securities and company shares above EUR 50,000 a year between relatives must be notified within three months (fine up to 10% of value if deliberately not reported).
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Gift notification duty (§ 121a BAO): gifts between relatives up to EUR 50,000 per donor and recipient in one year are exempt from notification; real estate is notified under the real estate transfer tax act instead.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Transfers to a private foundation bear 2.5% foundation entry tax (Stiftungseingangssteuer). Inherited real estate: real estate transfer tax (stepped, family rates, aggregated over 5 years) plus 1.1% registration fee on the property value (Grundstückswert). Political proposals to reintroduce inheritance tax are not enacted.
open_questions: The 2.5% foundation entry tax was not checked against the StiftEG text in this session.
children_treatment is 'fully_exempt' for the portfolio; real estate transfer tax of up to 3.5% plus 1.1% fee applies to inherited Austrian real estate, which the schema cannot express separately.
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax. Gifts above EUR 50,000 a year between relatives must be notified to the tax office within three months; gifts of real estate bear real estate transfer tax (0.5%/2%/3.5% stepped) plus 1.1% registration fee.
inheritance.business_relief: Not needed for inheritance tax. Real estate transfer tax on business transfers has a EUR 900,000 allowance (from general knowledge, not verified).
inheritance.foreign_assets: No tax on foreign assets either; foreign inheritance/gift tax of the situs country may apply.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Not relevant; there is no inheritance tax. The gift notification duty applies if donor or recipient lives in Austria.

residency.tax_residency_test: Unlimited liability with a home (Wohnsitz) in Austria, or habitual abode after a stay of more than six months. Treaty tie-breakers apply for dual residents.

routes.name: EU/EEA/Swiss free movement
routes.requirements: Registration of residence; registration certificate (Anmeldebescheinigung) after three months, with proof of sufficient funds and health insurance.

routes.name: Settlement permit except gainful employment (Niederlassungsbewilligung - ausgenommen Erwerbstätigkeit)
routes.requirements: For people of independent means who will not work in Austria: proof of substantial regular income, accommodation and health insurance; subject to an annual quota and German language requirements. Austria has no golden visa; citizenship by investment is discretionary and rare. Details not verified in this session.

corporate.summary: Corporate income tax 23%. Dividends from domestic and qualifying foreign participations are generally exempt; international participations of at least 10% held for one year are also exempt on gains (unless opted out). Distributions to individuals bear 27.5% withholding.

sources.title: Austria - Corporate - Taxes on corporate income

Asking rents (Austrian listings usually quote gross rent incl. operating costs and VAT). Checked 2026-10-15 against the upper-middle-class standard.

data.us_citizen_notes: The US-Austria income tax treaty and the 1982 US-Austria estate and gift tax treaty apply. Austria's 27.5% on gains and dividends is generally creditable against US tax on foreign-source income; non-US funds can be PFICs.
open_questions: Special regime considered and not modelled: the § 103 EStG immigration relief (Zuzugsbegünstigung) is granted only to scientists, researchers, artists and athletes whose move is in the public interest, and its percentage relief applies to foreign income in narrow cases; not realistic for a family office.
Residence permit details for non-EU nationals (quota, income threshold) were not verified; the migration.gv.at page was unavailable.
Treaty counts are from general knowledge.

income.name: Austria

income_tax.summary: Austria taxes residents on worldwide income with seven brackets for 2026: 0% to EUR 13,539, then 20%, 30%, 40%, 48%, 50% above EUR 104,859 and 55% above EUR 1 million. There is no municipal income tax in Vienna. Employees pay 18.07% social insurance up to a monthly ceiling of EUR 6,930; the self-employed (GSVG) pay 18.5% pension, 6.8% health and 1.53% self-employed provision on income up to EUR 8,085 a month.

employment_deduction.note: Standard allowance for employment income (Werbungskostenpauschale) of EUR 132. The 6% rate on the 13th/14th salary is not modelled.

source.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries - Austria - Individual - Deductions

income_tax.self_employed_notes: GSVG 2026 for Gewerbetreibende: pension 18.5% + health 6.8% + self-employed provision 1.53% = 26.83% of the contribution base (income-tax profit plus the contributions), plus accident insurance EUR 12.95 a month. Monthly maximum base EUR 8,085 (EUR 97,020 a year, contributions max EUR 2,182.17 a month); minimum base EUR 551.10 a month. Contributions are provisional until the final tax assessment. Free professions have different schemes.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax. Employee rate 18.07% = sickness 3.87 + unemployment 2.95 + pension 10.25 + miscellaneous 1.00 on the monthly ceiling EUR 6,930 (EUR 13,860 more on special payments, taxed at 17.07%). The 13th and 14th salary are taxed at 6% above an EUR 620 exemption (rates 6% to 55%), not at the scale above. Brackets are the PwC 2026 table.

sources.title: Austria - Individual - Taxes on personal income
PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries - Austria - Individual - Deductions

open_questions: Employee ceiling shown as annual EUR 97,020 = EUR 6,930 x 14 payments; special payments are subject to a separate annual ceiling (EUR 13,860).

regimes.name: Aufenthaltsbewilligung - Selbständiger (temporary self-employed permit)
regimes.description: Austria has no dedicated digital nomad permit. The self-employed residence permit needs a contractual obligation to carry out a specific self-employed activity for a client in Austria for more than six months, plus passport, housing, full health insurance and proof of livelihood. It does not fit remote work for foreign clients. Tax treatment is ordinary.
regimes.duration_note: Permit validity not stated on the opened page; extension must be applied for no earlier than three months before expiry.
open_questions: No official source found for a separate nomad permit; a 'Digital Nomad' permit mentioned by third-party sites could not be confirmed.

rent_1bed_monthly.description: Numbeo average monthly rent for a 1-bedroom city-centre apartment, Vienna; crowd-sourced, 1495 entries from 243 contributors in the past 12 months, last updated 14 October 2026. Unfurnished/furnished not distinguished. Numbeo gives only 1-bedroom and 3-bedroom figures, so no 2-bedroom value is recorded.

source.title: Cost of living in Vienna (rent prices)

costs.notes: Numbeo commenters say central Vienna figures look low. ImmoScout24.at puts the Q1 2026 median asking rent in Vienna at EUR 22.41 per m2 (gross, all dwellings), which implies higher rents than Numbeo for new lettings; not converted into a monthly rent. Check pass 2026-10-15: no reachable source for a 2-bedroom rent (see dossier change log).

income.residence_routes: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens move freely and register after three months. Non-EU nationals staying over six months need a residence title; there is no digital nomad permit. The temporary self-employed permit needs an Austrian client contract over six months. Skilled employees use the Rot-Weiß-Rot Card or EU Blue Card (salary thresholds not verified from an opened source).
open_questions: Official 2026 Rot-Weiß-Rot Card and Blue Card salary minima not verified.
No source for a 2-bedroom rent in Vienna.

succession.name: Austria
succession.summary: Children and the spouse are guaranteed half of their intestate share (Pflichtteil), and a will cannot remove it. A foreign national habitually resident in Austria can choose the law of their nationality under the EU Succession Regulation. Austria has no trust law, but a Privatstiftung (private foundation) can be set up under the PSG.
succession.reserved_share: Descendants and spouse or registered partner: a Pflichtteil of half their statutory share, paid in money (ABGB sections 756-759; parents and other ascendants no longer protected since the 2017 reform).
succession.foreign_law_note: Reg. 650/2012 art. 22 lets a person choose the law of their nationality for the whole estate; without a choice, the law of last habitual residence applies (art. 21). A choice of foreign law removes the Austrian Pflichtteil, subject to the public-policy exception (art. 35).
succession.trust_note: Austria has no domestic trust law and is not party to the Hague Trusts Convention. The HCCH status table lists no signature or ratification for this state; the Convention is not in force here. Foreign trusts are treated in practice as contractual or fiduciary arrangements. Transfers to a Privatstiftung (Privatstiftungsgesetz 1993) are taxed under the Stiftungseingangssteuergesetz, which also reaches comparable foreign foundations.
open_questions: Austrian tax treatment of foreign trusts (Stiftungseingangssteuergesetz scope, income tax on distributions) was not examined in detail.
Exact ABGB section numbers for the 2017 Pflichtteil rules were taken from memory plus general guides and should be checked at ris.bka.gv.at.

sources.title: ABGB (Austrian Civil Code), Federal Law Gazette database RIS
HCCH status table: 1985 Trusts Convention

immigration.name: Austria
immigration.summary: EU citizens register and get an Anmeldebescheinigung after three months. Austria has no golden visa. Non-EU people of independent means can apply for a Niederlassungsbewilligung - ausgenommen Erwerbstaetigkeit (the 'Privatier' permit): it needs a free place in a small annual quota (385 in 2025) and monthly income of twice the pension compensation rate (twice EUR 1,308.39 in 2026). Citizenship for 'extraordinary merit' (Section 10(6)) is discretionary and not sold at a fixed price.
immigration.naturalisation: Ordinarily 10 years of legal residence (reported, with at least 5 as a permanent resident), German at B2, secure income, no criminal record, and a citizenship test. A reform was announced for 2026; its content was not found. From secondary sources and background knowledge, not an official page.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Austria generally requires giving up the previous citizenship, with exceptions (for example descendants of Nazi-persecution victims, or citizenship granted for extraordinary merit in the state's interest). Not verified on an official page.

routes.name: EU/EEA/Swiss free movement
routes.summary: EU citizens register and receive an Anmeldebescheinigung after three months; no permit.
routes.requirements: Directive 2004/38/EC, implemented in the NAG. Non-workers need sufficient funds and health insurance. Permanent residence after 5 years.

routes.name: Settlement permit except gainful employment (Privatier)
routes.summary: Residence for people of independent means who will not work in Austria, subject to a small annual quota.
routes.requirements: Section 44 NAG: a free place in the annual quota (Privatiers: 385 places in the draft 2025 regulation; 2026 figure not found); fixed regular monthly income of at least twice the Ausgleichszulage Richtsatz of Section 293 ASVG (twice EUR 1,308.39 for a single person in 2026, so at least EUR 2,616.78 a month; the number of annual payments used was not confirmed); accommodation, health insurance, no public-funds burden; German language at A1 before the permit under the integration rules (not verified).
routes.physical_presence: Live in Austria; the permit does not allow gainful employment
routes.family: Family reunification possible; quota rules not sourced.
routes.tax_note: Austrian unlimited tax liability follows domicile or habitual abode, not the permit.

sources.title: Section 44 NAG: Niederlassungsbewilligung - ausgenommen Erwerbstaetigkeit (RIS consolidated)
Explanatory notes to the Settlement Ordinance (BMI)

routes.name: Citizenship for extraordinary merit (Section 10(6) StbG)
routes.summary: Discretionary citizenship for exceptional achievements in art, science, economy or sport that serve the Republic's interest; large investment alone is not enough.
routes.requirements: Government decision (no appeal); achievements must clearly exceed the norm; the grant must be in Austria's interest. Commentators discuss figures from EUR 3 million to 10 million with no fixed price and no guarantee; none is official. Requires no prior residence and may allow keeping the old nationality.
routes.tax_note: Citizenship does not set tax residence.

routes.name: EU Blue Card and Red-White-Red Card (work)
routes.summary: Employer-sponsored permits for skilled workers, key workers and graduates.
routes.requirements: EU Blue Card: reported gross annual salary EUR 55,678 for 2026 (14 payments), degree of at least three years, job offer of at least 6 months; valid up to 24 months, then Red-White-Red Card plus. Other key workers: EUR 3,465 gross a month in 2026. Secondary sources only.
routes.tax_note: Taxed as resident if domicile or habitual abode is in Austria.

sources.title: The EU Blue Card: an overview

open_questions: Privatier permit: 2026 quota number, number of ASVG payments for the monthly threshold (12 or 14), language requirement and fees not found.
Blue Card EUR 55,678 and other key worker EUR 3,465: confirm on BMI / oesterreich.gv.at (secondary sources).
Naturalisation: official oesterreich.gv.at requirements and the announced 2026 reform; dual-citizenship exceptions.
Merit citizenship: no official criteria or amount; the process and any 2026 amendment unconfirmed.
No digital nomad or business-owner route recorded; Red-White-Red Card self-employed key workers not researched.
